text: DSH Usage & Credits 是面向 DSH 网页端的 API 额度与会话费用显示插件。它在对话输入框下方加入余额和会话支出提示，并在设置页提供汇率、币种与刷新选项。插件读取 DeepSeek 账户钱包余额，将人民币、美元和所选本地货币并列展示；同时按新输入、缓存写入、缓存命中和输出等 Token 用量估算当前会话费用，并考虑模型类型及高峰时段。汇率从多个公开来源获取并缓存。适合希望在 DSH 对话中查看账户余额和了解会话开销的 DeepSeek 用户；查看余额需要已登录账户。

DSH Usage & Credits adds balance and session cost displays to the DSH web client. Composer pills show DeepSeek wallet totals and estimate spend by token type, including cache hits. Settings show rates, offer local currency choices and refresh. A signed-in account is required for balance access.
想在 DSH 对话窗口里顺手看 DeepSeek 账户还剩多少额度。
有没有办法把 API 余额换算成我常用的本地货币？
我想知道一段 DSH 会话大概花了多少钱。
让 DSH 按缓存命中和新输入分别估算 Token 费用。
想在设置里切换消费金额的显示币种，并手动刷新余额和汇率。
How can I see my remaining DeepSeek credits while chatting in DSH?
I want an estimate of what each conversation costs, including cached tokens.
Can I display my balance and spend in a currency I use locally?
DSH Usage & Credits 的功能「额度余额」：在对话输入框下方显示 DeepSeek 钱包余额，并提供本地货币换算。打开 DSH 网页端后自动读取账户；余额详情也可在设置页查看。
DSH Usage & Credits 的功能「会话费用估算」：根据当前会话 Token 用量，分别计算新输入、缓存写入、缓存命中和输出费用，并显示在输入框下方；悬停可查看费用明细。
DSH Usage & Credits 的功能「汇率与币种设置」：设置页可选择本地货币或按账户充值币种显示会话费用，查看汇率来源和更新时间，并手动刷新余额与汇率。
DSH Usage & Credits 使用前须知：查看 DeepSeek 余额需要已登录账户；人民币汇率通过公开汇率服务获取，余额由账户服务读取。

@local/dsh-api-credits README · DSH Usage & Credits：A [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) plugin that shows your **API credit balance** and the **credit spend of the current session** right under the composer — in CNY, USD and your own local currency, at live exchange rates.

> The balance is what is left in your DeepSeek account. The spend is what this particular conversation has already consumed, priced by the actual billing buckets, including cache hits.

@local/dsh-api-credits README · What you get：| Where | What |
|---|---|
| Composer dock | `¥12.34 ($1.85, 151 ₽)` — topped-up balance: yuan first, then dollars and your local currency |
| Composer dock | `−¥0.65` — session spend, with a receipt icon; hover for the full breakdown |
| Tooltip | Rate source, `¥1 = … ₽`, `$1 = … ¥`, refresh time, cache state, which providers answered |
| Settings → API Credits | Balance in its native wallets (`¥12.34 + $1.85`), the local-currency equivalent, local currency picker, spend-currency switch, rate details, refresh button |
@local/dsh-api-credits README · What you get：The balance pill follows the same visual language as DSH's own `N tok` pills: same row, same spacing, same typography, theme tokens only.

section: Why the spend is not "tokens × price"

text:
@local/dsh-api-credits README · Why the spend is not "tokens × price"：The plugin prices each bucket separately, straight from the session's `tokenUsage` projection:

```
cost = (uncachedInput + cacheWrite) × miss
     + cacheRead                     × hit
     + output                        × output
     × (peak ? 2 : 1)

Real numbers from a 13.9M-token session with a 99% cache hit rate: **¥0.65**, while "everything at miss price" would claim ¥27.80 — a 42× overestimate.
section: Why the spend is not "tokens × price"

text:
@local/dsh-api-credits README · Pricing：Official DeepSeek prices per 1M tokens. Off-peak is listed first, peak hours cost exactly double:

| Model | Currency | Cache hit | Cache miss | Output |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `deepseek-flash` | CNY | 0.02 / 0.04 | 1 / 2 | 4 / 8 |
| `deepseek-flash` | USD | 0.003 / 0.006 | 0.15 / 0.30 | 0.60 / 1.20 |
| `deepseek-v4-pro` | CNY | 0.15 / 0.30 | 4.5 / 9 | 13.5 / 27 |
| `deepseek-v4-pro` | USD | 0.022 / 0.044 | 0.66 / 1.32 | 1.98 / 3.96 |

@local/dsh-api-credits README · Pricing：Both price lists are kept natively, so a dollar wallet is not billed through a CNY conversion. The model family is detected from the routes recorded in the session.

@local/dsh-api-credits README · Pricing：**Peak** is 01:00–04:00 and 06:00–10:00 UTC on weekdays (09:00–12:00 and 14:00–18:00 Beijing time); everything else, including weekends, is off-peak. Chinese public holidays are not modelled — those days are priced as peak, i.e. deliberately on the safe side. The band is taken at render time, so a session spanning a peak boundary is estimated with one band.

@local/dsh-api-credits README · Settings：* **Local currency** — 60 common fiat currencies (RUB by default, KZT, BYN, EUR, GEL, AMD, TRY, AED, INR, JPY, KRW, …). Names come from `Intl.DisplayNames`, symbols from `Intl.NumberFormat`, so nothing is hardcoded per currency.
* **Session spend in** — `Local` (converted from the CNY price list at the live cross-rate, with the CNY equivalent shown in the tooltip) or `Top-up` (the currency of the largest wallet, CNY or USD, priced from its own official list).
@local/dsh-api-credits README · Settings：Both choices are stored in `localStorage`, per browser.

@local/dsh-api-credits README · Exchange rates：The yuan is the primary currency. Every provider is asked for a full "units per 1 ¥" table, so any of the listed currencies can be local. All providers are queried at once and the **first valid answer wins**; the rest are aborted.

@local/dsh-api-credits README · Exchange rates：| id | Endpoint |
|---|---|
| `cbr` | `cbr-xml-daily.ru/daily_json.js` — Bank of Russia, cross-rates derived from its table |
| `jsdelivr` | `cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@fawazahmed0/currency-api` |
| `erapi` | `open.er-api.com/v6/latest/CNY` |
| `fxratesapi` | `api.fxratesapi.com/latest?base=CNY` |
| `exchangerate` | `api.exchangerate-api.com/v4/latest/CNY` |
| `floatrates` | `floatrates.com/daily/cny.json` |

@local/dsh-api-credits README · Exchange rates：A payload is accepted only when `0.05 < $/¥ < 0.4`, it lists at least three currencies, and — when the rouble is present — `3 < ₽/¥ < 40`. The winning rate is cached for 6 hours, refreshed every 30 minutes and when the window regains focus; if the network is gone, the last known rate is shown with a “cached” marker. No rate is ever hardcoded.

@local/dsh-api-credits README · Where the balance comes from：1. `ctx.remote.account.getBalance()` — the same authenticated channel the Settings → Account page uses. Note that a dynamic client plugin cannot reach it through `ctx.remote.account` (the sandbox proxies the service, not the namespace tree); `ctx.get('remote.account')` is the working path, and the plugin also tolerates the namespace mounting late.
2. A loopback route `/api-credits/balance` served by the Host half, guarded by a per-process token that the Host injects into the page it serves. Requests without the token get `403`.

@local/dsh-api-credits README · Where the balance comes from：Either way the balance never leaves your machine: the browser talks to your local DSH host, which talks to the DeepSeek platform with your own credentials.

@local/dsh-api-credits README · Install：The repository root **is** the bundle, and the package is a normal pnpm dependency, so a GitHub ref and a local checkout both work. In Desktop, open the Plugin Manager and install it straight from the repository link — `https://github.com/exterme-russian-dsh-fandom/dsh-usage-credits` — or from a shell:

text:
@local/dsh-api-credits README · from a local checkout：A local checkout is linked rather than copied, so `git pull` there reaches the running plugin after a page reload; a Git install is a fetched copy, and moving it to a newer ref means reinstalling.

The bundle patch inserts one row, `api-credits`. It has no dependencies and no build step: the Host half registers the token-guarded balance route, the Client half registers both dock pills and the Settings page.
@local/dsh-api-credits README · from a local checkout：Requires a signed-in DeepSeek account for the balance; without one the plugin shows a sign-in hint and still displays the rate.

@local/dsh-api-credits README · Layout：```
package.json        bundle manifest: dsh.bundle.patch + dsh.client
cordis.patch.yml    inserts the `api-credits` row
index.js            Host half: token-guarded balance route, index injection
client.js           Client half: rate store, two dock pills, settings page

@local/dsh-api-credits README · Limitations：* Prices are a snapshot of the official price list; DeepSeek may change them. They live in one `PRICES` table in `client.js`.
* Peak-band estimation ignores Chinese public holidays and treats a session as if it ran entirely in the current band.
* Settings are stored per browser, not in the profile.
* Balance and spend are estimates for your own accounting; the authoritative number is the one Platform charges.
